courses.description: Students will build a foundation in classic world literature and find thematic and archetypal connections with more modern literature. We will also practice reading for a variety of purposes. Students will practice writing and revising for various purposes, including argumentative writing, informative/ explanatory, and narratives. Students will conduct short and sustained research projects to combine elements of learning targets. Students will practice and perform language learning objectives within class and through writing assignments.
courses.fulfills_text: 9th Grade Requirement

courses.description: In American Voices, we will explore writing from across the United States, reflecting diverse American perspectives, writing styles, eras, and genres. We will make connections to historical events and themes, such as the Native American and immigrant experiences, the Great Migration, and the complicated promise of ‘the American Dream.’ Inspired by what we read, we will build our own writing, speaking, and collaboration skills.
courses.fulfills_text: 10th Grade Requirement

courses.description: Wayfinding is a course designed to assist students in exploring options for life after high school. Whether you’re thinking about joining the workforce, are college bound, taking a gap year, traveling abroad, or you’re not at all sure of your direction, this course will open up possibilities and help to guide you towards your path. Students will engage in multiple activities such as interest inventories, personality tests, a reality game, a values auction, and a values assessment in order to help align them with possible career paths. There are multiple opportunities to hone verbal communication skills, such as through informational interviews and presentations. Students will read Tuesdays with Morrie and The Last Lecture.

Take a college-level writing course on Hazen’s campus! It will either be in expository writing (narrative and informational essays) or in creative writing, covering fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction. Either way, become a better writer and get ready to become the great writer that you will be later in life.

Take a college-level writing course. It will either be in expository writing (narrative and informational essays) or in creative writing, covering fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction. Either way, become a better writer and get ready to become the great writer that you will be later in life.

Reading and Writing to Challenge the Status Quo: This class will center around themes of censorship and intellectual freedom as students read and analyze literature of a variety of genres, including contemporary novels, historical fiction, science fiction,fantasy and literature with futuristic views of the world. We will examine how literature often critiques the society we live in, and gives much food for thought on why we do the things we do, and maybe why we should change those things. We will study the author's craft, design and structure, and analyze the text to better understand how master authors write to communicate messages.Students will have opportunities to create their own reading lists and personalize their learning around social issues and actions of importance to them.

This course will be a broad survey of philosophical topics, such as logical reasoning & argumentation, truth & knowledge, and ethics. The course will involve a great deal of discussion, debate, and persuasive writing.

Dare To Be Me is for students who like to be active, get outside, breathe fresh air, and engage their hearts, senses, bodies, and minds. As its title suggests, the focus of the course is on being rather than doing. By blending time in Nature with physical exercise, mindfulness, quiet introspection, meaningful, in-depth conversations and creative journaling, DTBM students learn to understand themselves better and develop the courage to lean into who they want to become. They will grow their ability to be present, curious, grateful, empathetic, adaptable and resilient even in times of adversity while identifying their passions, advancing their emotional literacy, and beginning to articulate and embody their values and purpose. The class prioritizes holistic wellbeing and self-discovery and is built on the philosophy that students who are self-aware, grounded, and balanced can access any kind of learning at a much deeper level. It is therefore a perfect complement to any other class while teaching essential life and transferable skills.
courses.fulfills_text: .5 English & .5 PE
courses.notes: Specialty program; Semester - 2 Blocks. Final approval is dependent on instructor permission based on application letter and/or interview. Earns .5 English and .5 PE credit.

courses.description: World History I begins with an examination of the social and environmental reasons that human beings began to form civilizations. The era of prehistory and the early river valley civilizations will be explored in this course. Students discover the contributions and the impacts that these early civilizations produced. As empires begin to emerge the focus shifts beyond tangible contributions to notions of government, religion, and culture that evolve from these more advanced regions of the world. Global awareness is a large piece of this course. Students will identify many locations and understand the influence that these regions and their resources have on the people who have inhabited them. World History I focuses on the impact that history has on the world that we live in today. There will be regular reading assignments, class discussion, homework, quizzes, and tests. There is a component of modern world issues built into this course.
courses.fulfills_text: 9th Grade Requirement

courses.description: World History II continues to teach where World History I leaves off. The focus of the content covered is on the era of the Renaissance, different revolutions, significant people, and the causes and effects of social and political change. Certain areas allow for explorations of topics that connect directly to modern day issues that better inform students about their world around them. The focus question of the course is: How will the past affect the decisions that people make as participants in global change and continuity. The course is based mostly on an inquiry based method of teaching. There will be regular reading assignments, class discussion, homework, quizzes, tests, and research enhanced papers. There is a component of modern world issues built into this course.
courses.fulfills_text: 9th Grade Requirement

courses.description: The purpose of this course is to build and expand on historical reading, writing, and thinking skills within the context of US History. Students will study and analyze themes in history from influential eras of American culture, such as the Civil War, the Gilded Age, the Roaring ’20s, WWI, the Great Depression, and WWII. Anticipated themes include, but are not limited to, identity, politics and power, technology, culture and society, migration, geography and the environment, and globalization.
courses.fulfills_text: 10th Grade Requirement

courses.description: The purpose of this course is to build on and expand on historical reading, writing, and thinking skills within the context of US History. Students will study and analyze themes in history from influential eras of US History including, but not limited to, the Cold War, Civil Rights, Counterculture, Rise of Conservatism, and Globalization. Anticipated themes include, but are not limited to, identity, politics and power, technology, culture and society, migration, geography and the environment, and globalization.
courses.fulfills_text: 10th Grade Requirement

courses.description: In this semester-long class we will revisit the basics of American Government and its history, explore our government system at a higher-level understanding and you will demonstrate your abilities to function as an active citizen of our communities and the United States as you approach and reach the age in which you have the privilege and responsibility to vote.
courses.fulfills_text: Fulfills Government Requirement

courses.description: A survey of issues facing the world and their potential impacts on our communities.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of 9th & 10th Grade History

courses.description: This course is a general survey of the important concepts in psychology concerning traditional theories and modern developments. It explores the following foundational topics: history of psychology, the different perspectives of psychology, neuroscience, APA code of ethics, states of consciousness, and resilience.

Project-based course that blends the fundamentals of economics with real-world, hands-on learning. Students will explore key concepts in microeconomics and macroeconomics—such as supply and demand, opportunity cost, economic systems, labor, entrepreneurship, and sustainability—through tangible projects rooted in our local Hardwick economy and do-it-yourself culture. Through activities like small engine repair, creating and marketing homemade goods, repurposing discarded items, community interviews, and simulating small business ventures, students will gain a practical understanding of how economic systems function at both the household and community levels. Emphasis will be placed on critical thinking, resourcefulness, collaboration, and innovation. Whether repairing or building a simple product to sell or investigating how local businesses thrive, students will learn to see economics not just as abstract theory but as a powerful tool for problem-solving, self-sufficiency, and positive community impact.
courses.prerequisites: None

courses.description: This is an accelerated high school history course designed to meet the criteria for an entry-level college course within the political science discipline. At the end of the course, students will have the opportunity to take the AP exam - a standardized test that measures how well students have learned the content and skills of an AP course. A passing score (3-5) may gain your student college credit at select colleges. Taking an AP course provides an opportunity for the curious and serious to gain familiarity with a college curriculum and work expectations as well as dig deeper into the debates and issues surrounding United States Government & Politics.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of US History with a proficiency of 3 or higher

courses.description: Learn the basics of budgeting, borrowing, and investing and how these can affect your future. What you know about money will determine how well prepared you are for buying a house or car, raising a family, enjoying your leisure time, and having a financially secure retirement. Some of the topics to be covered in this class will include: savings accounts, investments, loans, credit/debit cards, credit ratings, taxes, and insurance.
courses.prerequisites: Completed two years of high school math

courses.description: Students will gain basic number literacy needed to be able to be successful in Algebra I. This will include working with integers, fractions, decimals, exponents, and square roots. Students will also work with surface area and volume of three-dimensional figures, as well as find missing side lengths of right triangles using the Pythagorean Theorem. Students will then cover how to find the probability of simple events. Students will also cover some Algebra I topics such as simplifying numeric and algebraic expressions, and solving and graphing equations and inequalities.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation from teacher

courses.description: This class will cover one-variable and two-variable algebra, including simplifying numeric and algebraic expressions and solving equations and inequalities. Additionally, linear functions, systems of linear equations, linear inequalities, quadratic (and power family) functions and exponential functions will be covered. Instructional practices include a mix of direct instruction and inquiry-based activities. The use of technology is integrated throughout the course.
courses.prerequisites: Mathematics 8, Integrated Math, Pre-Algebra or recommendation from teacher

courses.description: This class will cover basic geometric vocabulary and formulas, including measurement of angles and lengths, two- and three-dimensional figures, relationships in and among triangles and congruence and similarity. Later, the class will cover parallel lines, triangle congruence and similarity, right triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, and transformations. Instructional practices include a mix of direct instruction and inquiry-based activities. The use of technology is integrated throughout the course. A classroom set of TI-84+ graphing calculators is available; however, it is expected that students will have access to a scientific calculator for homework. Students will receive more information in regard to calculators at the beginning of the course.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I

courses.description: This course covers the algebraic manipulations of polynomial, exponential, trigonometric, and composite functions. It also covers systems of equations and includes an introduction to matrices. The use of technology is integrated throughout the course. In order to foster skills needed in subsequent classes and on standardized tests, TI-84 graphing calculators will be used and supplied daily.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I and Geometry

courses.description: This course covers polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions. Functions are presented in multiple ways and in more depth than in Algebra II. It also covers introductory Calculus topics if time allows. Lessons will primarily include direct instruction. The use of technology is integrated throughout the course. It is expected that students will have access to a TI-83 or TI-84 graphing calculator for homework. Students will receive more information in regard to purchasing or leasing calculators at the beginning of the course.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I, Algebra II, and Geometry

courses.description: This class will cover major introductory topics in probability (including simple and compound probability, combinations/permutations, theoretical and experimental probabilities, and expected value) and in statistics (including measures of central tendency, statistical bias, and data analysis.) It is recommended for students who may struggle with the full Probability & Statistics course and for students who are considering attending GMTCC. It is expected that students will have access to a scientific calculator for homework. Students will receive more information in regards to calculators at the beginning of the course.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I and currently enrolled in Geometry

courses.description: An introduction to the basic ideas and techniques of probability and statistics. Topics may include numerical and graphical descriptive measures, probability, random variables, the normal distribution, sampling theory, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. The use of technology may be required. Students must take a math assessment for placement purposes prior to registration.

The main objective of this course is to have students develop a solid conceptual understanding of the following four major concepts: limits, derivatives, indefinite integrals, and definite integrals. Students will develop this understanding by approaching and solving problems verbally, graphically, numerically, and analytically. Much emphasis will be placed on student presentation of solutions in writing as well as orally justifying their processes to the class. Daily collaboration is an essential part of success in this course. Graphing calculators will be used extensively throughout the course. It is strongly recommended that students purchase their own graphing calculator. All students who sign up for the class will take the AP Exam.
courses.prerequisites: Pre-Calculus

courses.description: Students will participate in hands-on activities and group and classroom discussions to gain a basic understanding of scientific concepts in many areas. These will include, but are not limited to energy and energy transfers and transformations, climate and climate change, resource and resource management, atmosphere and space, chemistry, and what it takes to support human life on a planet.
courses.fulfills_text: 9th Grade Requirement

courses.description: This is a sophomore level course that addresses the NGSS life science standards and builds on the NGSS crosscutting concepts and science practices that all OSSU students work on every year in science classes.
courses.fulfills_text: 10th Grade Requirement

courses.description: This course is a standards-based study of fundamental chemical concepts, such as atomic theory and its relation to physical and chemical behavior of matter, chemical bonding, the mole and stoichiometry, molecular kinetics, and acids-bases. Emphasis is placed on the utilization of mathematical, analytical, data acquisition, and communication skills. Concepts and skills are reinforced by a strong emphasis on hands-on laboratory experiences and the integration of other branches of science.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I

courses.description: In this class you will learn the History of Astronomy, rockets and space exploration. You will also study celestial objects and phenomena applying mathematics, physics, chemistry, and engineering in an effort to explain those objects and phenomena. You will learn to build rockets and telescopes and the science behind these. You will learn about Earth’s place in the Universe and the Solar System. You will learn about Galaxies, the Universe and the evolution of all these topics. Students will also learn and discuss ongoing and recent news in Astronomy.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I
courses.notes: Length listed as '½ or Full Year'

courses.description: Students will participate in individual and group hands-on activities to solve engineering challenges using the design-build-test-revise engineering model. These will include, but are not limited to problems in mechanics, electrical systems, computer programming, and complex systems involving multiple challenges such as robotics. This class may be repeated.
This course is designed to empower students to feel more comfortable in public speaking situations through targeted assignments, practice and feedback.
courses.fulfills_text: Waivers for Participation in Drama or Student Council: Participation with a speaking role in a minimum of three separate shows or presentations allows students to earn 1/2 credit of performance arts, fulfilling the requirement.

courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with an introduction to Spanish language and Hispanic cultures. Students will acquire novice-mid level competence in interpretive, interpersonal and presentational modes of communication. These three modes of communication will support intercultural learning and interdisciplinary and personal connections. Students and teacher will build community through use of Spanish language in games, stories, music, films, etc. Students will be assessed using the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) proficiencies. The proficiency level for this level 1 class is novice-mid. At this level, students will be able to communicate on familiar topics using words, short phrases and simple sentences. This course provides a basis for continued acquisition of Spanish, English and other languages while expanding students’ intercultural awareness and strengthening their identities in the global community.

This course is sequential to Spanish I and will reinforce the proficiencies previously achieved. Students will acquire a novice-high level of competence in interpretive, interpersonal and presentational modes of communication. These three modes of communication will support intercultural learning and interdisciplinary and personal connections. Students and teacher will build community through use of Spanish language in games, stories, music, films, etc. Students will be assessed using the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) proficiencies. The proficiency level for this level 2 class is novice-high. At this level, students will be able to communicate on common topics using short phrases and sentences. This course provides a basis for continued acquisition of Spanish, English and other languages while expanding students’ intercultural awareness and strengthening their identities in the global community.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Spanish I or 7th and 8th grade Spanish, or permission of instructor

courses.description: Sequential to Spanish II, this course will reinforce the proficiencies previously achieved. Students will acquire an intermediate-low level of competence in interpretive, interpersonal and presentational modes of communication. These three modes of communication will support intercultural learning and interdisciplinary and personal connections. Students and teacher will build community through use of Spanish language in games, stories, music, films, etc. Students will be assessed using the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) proficiencies. The proficiency level for this level 3 class is intermediate-low. At this level, students will be able to communicate and elaborate on common topics using short phrases and simple sentences. This course will draw on students' previous acquisition for continued development in Spanish, English and other languages while expanding students’ intercultural awareness and strengthening their identities in the global community.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Spanish II or permission of instructor

courses.description: Sequential to Spanish III, this course will reinforce the proficiencies previously achieved. Students will acquire an intermediate-mid level of competence in interpretive, interpersonal and presentational modes of communication. These three modes of communication will support intercultural learning and interdisciplinary and personal connections. Students and teacher will build community through use of Spanish language in games, stories, music, films, etc. Students will be assessed using the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) proficiencies. The proficiency level for this level 4 class is intermediate-low. At this level, students will be able to communicate, give details and elaborate on common topics using sentences, often at the paragraph level. This course will draw on students' previous acquisition for continued development in Spanish, English and other languages while expanding students’ intercultural awareness and strengthening their identities in the global community.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Spanish III or permission of instructor

courses.description: Sequential to Spanish IV, this course will reinforce the proficiencies previously achieved. Students will acquire an intermediate-high level of competence in interpretive, interpersonal and presentational modes of communication. These three modes of communication will support intercultural learning and interdisciplinary and personal connections. Students and teacher will build community through use of Spanish language in games, stories, music, films, etc. Students will be assessed using the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) proficiencies. The proficiency level for this level 5 class is intermediate-mid. At this level, students will be able to narrate, describe and explain common topics using sentences, often at the paragraph level. This course will draw on students' previous acquisition for continued development in Spanish, English and other languages while expanding students’ intercultural awareness and strengthening their identities in the global community.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Spanish IV or permission of instructor

courses.description: This introductory ceramics course for grades 9–12 provides students with a foundational understanding of clay as an artistic medium through exploration of hand-building and introductory wheel-throwing techniques with some various cultural history around clay usages. Students will primarily focus on hand-built projects such as functional pinch and coil vessels, slab-constructed ceramic containers or forms, and a sculptural project that emphasizes form, texture, and personal expression. Students will also have the opportunity to experience basic pottery wheel techniques as an introduction to wheel-thrown forms. Throughout the course, students will learn essential skills including clay preparation, joining techniques, surface decoration, glazing methods, and kiln safety. Instruction aligns with National Core Arts Standards by encouraging students to generate and conceptualize artistic ideas (VA:Cr1), organize and develop artistic work through skill-building and craftsmanship (VA:Cr2), refine and complete works of art through reflection and revision (VA:Cr3), and analyze and interpret their own work and the work of others while connecting ceramics to cultural and historical contexts (VA:Re7, VA:Cn11). Students will build technical skills, creative confidence, and an understanding of ceramics as both a functional and expressive art form.

Each week you will be posting your photographs to a discussion board to share with the class. We will be building a lively and interactive community of photographers. It is essential that you participate in the discussions - this is where you will share not only your photographs, but your ideas and learning as well. Photography - and art in general - is about learning craft, design, history, culture, and self expression. You will synthesize these elements to create a portfolio of work that reflects your newly developed skills as well as a general appreciation for art. **The course is designed to use a camera on an iPhone or Android phone.**

Any person interested in the field of art will benefit from this course. Drawing is the basis of all the other visual arts: painting, sculpture, architecture, illustration, fashion design, and even stage productions. This drawing course is directed towards individual student needs and interests, whether a student is working on an art school entry portfolio or just enjoys drawing. This course provides the basics of composition and technique. Students may choose from a wide variety of drawing materials.

This course introduces students to the use of pencil, charcoal, pen and ink, pastels and other drawing mediums with a focus on observational drawing skills. Students will develop a deeper understanding of drawing as a new way of seeing, problem solving, organizing ideas, and recording perceptions of the world around them. This course will be taught as a Dual Enrollment course with CCV. Students will receive 1 high school credit and 3 college credits.

Any person interested in the field of art will benefit from this course. Drawing is the basis of all the other visual arts: painting, sculpture, architecture, illustration, fashion design, and even stage productions. This drawing course is directed towards individual student needs and interests, whether a student is working on an art school entry portfolio or just enjoys drawing. This course provides the basics of composition and technique. Students may choose from a wide variety of drawing materials.

During the 1st semester of class, students will work with watercolor paint to understand various watercolor painting techniques and brush strokes. Students will create a series of small paintings of flowers, leaves, architecture and a still life. During the 2nd semester of class, students explore advanced techniques and processes with acrylic paint and will create paintings to submit in various art contests and public art events, including the Junior Duck Stamp Contest and the Young American Patriotic Art Contest. Having strong drawing skills is necessary with both watercolor and acrylic painting.
courses.prerequisites: Introduction to Studio Art or Art I

courses.description: This class is for serious student-artists who have a positive attitude, a strong work ethic, and an in-depth understanding of the elements and principles of design. Students in this course must be self-motivated and dedicated to the course and their art in order to succeed, and they must be open to criticism. Students will work more independently in this course and therefore will participate in strict deadlines and regular homework assignments. This course covers complex media, advanced still life and observational compositions, printmaking, and studies in mixed media and design concepts. The projects covered in this course should prepare students for the Advanced Placement Studio Art course or those planning to pursue art in college/career.
courses.prerequisites: Introduction to Studio Art, Illustration, or Printmaking

courses.description: This course is designed for students who are seriously interested in the practical experience of art on a college level. The Advanced Placement Studio Portfolio consists of two sections: Sustained Investigation and Selected Works. Both areas will be discussed and worked on in depth throughout the year in and out of class, as well as in the prerequisite of Studio Art Honors. Students will develop skills of creating compositions, developing concepts, and applying critical thinking and problem solving to their artwork. Students will complete in class projects as well as out of class assignments such as journals, sketchbooks, and writing assignments. This course enables the development of mastery in concept, composition, and execution of successful designs. The course will cover a variety of media and techniques and will encourage students to go outside of project guidelines and above project requirements.
courses.prerequisites: Introduction to Studio Art, Drawing or Printmaking, Studio Art Honors

courses.description: This course introduces students to the use of clay, paper mache, wood, assemblage and other sculpture mediums with a focus on the additive and subtractive process as well as mold making. Students will develop a deeper understanding of sculpture as a new way of seeing, problem solving, organizing ideas, and recording perceptions of the world around them.

A collaboratively-designed musical learning opportunity. From getting better at an instrument to learning about music production, from honing music theory chops to crafting the perfect song, this process-centered course can be molded to fit each student’s individual interests as a musician. Given the multiple pathways available within the course, students can take Music Expo more than once.

This class is offered to provide students with a group musical experience through ensemble playing in a Concert Band. We will play a variety of music and will work on growing skills as musicians and as people.

This class is offered to provide students with a group musical experience through ensemble singing in a Chorus. Concentration is on the performance of the highest quality choral literature and expanding the student’s musical knowledge. We will study a broad spectrum of works composed by many different composers from many time periods and cultures. We will develop the musicianship of all participants in a variety of creative ways. Through this course participants will explore various ways to use their instrument expressively and work to understand and apply the technique in a healthy manner. All students will work to grow in the course no matter the skill level. Live performances are an integral component of these courses and all students are expected to attend required performances (including parades for band members). The music department does take an annual field trip which all members are invited to attend.

This class is offered to provide students with an additional ensemble experience playing in a Jazz Band. Students will learn a variety of jazz music, as well as basic improvisational skills, and will work to grow as musicians and as people through this ensemble. If a student wants to join who plays guitar, piano, or bass, they should set up a meeting with the teacher.
courses.prerequisites: Enrolled in Concert Band

courses.description: This class is offered to students in pursuit of the highest level of musical artistry within the choral medium. Concentration is on the performance of the highest quality choral literature and expanding the student’s musical knowledge. We will study a broad spectrum of works composed by many different composers from many time periods, and cultures. We will develop the musicianship of all participants in a variety of creative ways. Through this course participants will explore various ways to use their voice expressively and work to understand and apply the voice in a healthy manner. All students will learn to sing better than when they came into the course. Live performances are an integral component of the course and all students are expected to attend required performances. The chorus does take an annual field trip which all members are invited to attend.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor Recommendation, Enrollment in Concert Chorus

courses.description: This semester-long course is designed to introduce and excite students about career pathways within the bicycle industry and prepare them for entry-level positions as bicycle technicians or retail associates. Skills are developed and assessed by a combination of hands-on tests, written assessments, presentations, and project-based learning. This course uses some of the NGSS standards as performance criteria. Upon successful completion of the course with a grade of three or better, students will be awarded the Bicycle Technology Level 1 industry endorsed certificate by establishing career readiness skills in combination with the professional technical skill standards.
courses.prerequisites: Basic reading, writing, and math skills

courses.description: This course is an introduction to learning the techniques and interrelationships found in design, manufacturing, and production. Instruction will focus on the critical actions, knowledge, systems, and processes necessary to participate in a design/manufacturing enterprise. Activities will focus on manufacturing processes and production, quality and continuous improvement practices, maintenance awareness, and safety. Students will develop high performance skills through demonstrations, lectures, self-paced studies, labs, technical presentations, critical thinking, problem-solving, and individual and group activities in order to demonstrate the core set of skills and knowledge necessary to prepare for sustained careers in a high performance environment.

This course will focus on individualized fitness and sports/physical performance training. Students will choose an area of interest in sports or fitness and personalize a training program to fit their needs.

This course will focus on the team strategies, skills, rules, conditioning drills and sportsmanship involved in a variety of team sports (ie, soccer, basketball, football, volleyball, etc). The goal for this course is that students will experience a variety of activities that promote wellness and physical and mental health in high school and beyond.
courses.fulfills_text: Waivers for Participation in Sports: Successful completion of four high school sports seasons allows students to earn 1/2 credit of physical education.
courses.notes: Can be repeated. Waivers for Participation in Sports: Successful completion of four high school sports seasons allows students to earn 1/2 credit of physical education.

courses.description: The goal of High School Health class is to promote health literacy, physical fitness and reduce health risks in students.
courses.fulfills_text: Required for Graduation

courses.description: A designated space in the school that offers a quiet, structured environment for students to complete schoolwork and potentially receive academic support from a trained adult. Offered to any student who is not otherwise assigned to an academic course.
courses.notes: Offered to any student who is not otherwise assigned to an academic course.

courses.description: A designated space in the school that offers a quiet, structured environment for students to complete schoolwork and potentially receive academic support from a trained adult. If you are hoping to meet with a specific teacher, please reach out to them directly in advance to ensure their availability.

This is an introductory course in student-driven exploration of a wide range of makerspace opportunities: from advanced manufacturing and engineering principles and techniques, industry and community to car engines and electricity, to creative arts like textile design or jewelry making. The course enables students to gain the necessary skills and knowledge to: self-identify their learning process and goals, explore careers in manufacturing and engineering technologies, grow team building skills in science fields and contexts, and construct independent-based learning opportunities in our community Makerspace.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I

courses.description: A Recipe for Human Connection explores our connections to food, sharing recipes, story-telling, harvesting, cooking, exploring the food knowledge of our elders, and creating space for our community to come together around food and gratitude. As the pandemic shifts our opportunities for connection, this project aims to create new opportunities to find joy and relationship through the creation and sharing of food.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I

courses.description: Driver Education is designed to teach safety practices involved in the use of a motor vehicle. Driver and Traffic Safety Education can teach decision making skills; how to cope with various traffic problems, what to do in adverse weather conditions/emergencies; responsibilities for passengers and other roadway users; basic car control, maneuvers, ownership, maintenance and how to plan a trip.
courses.credits_text: Students will receive 0.5 Elective credit for successfully completing Driver’s Ed
courses.prerequisites: Students must be in possession of a Vermont Learner's Permit by the first day of class in order to be in this course. It is requested that students drive a minimum of 10 hours with parents/guardians prior to class.
courses.notes: Offered the Fall Semester period 7 and Spring Semester after school with a limit of 50 students. Students receive 0.5 Elective credit for successfully completing Driver's Ed.

courses.description: EXPLORATORY PRE-TECHNOLOGY is designed for 10th grade students who thrive in a hands-on learning environment with an emphasis on applied academics. Students engage in traditional academic subjects, in addition to developing employability and technical skills necessary to be successful in a global workforce and pursuit of lifelong professional learning. Intensive career exploration opportunities occur in several programs, taking into consideration students’ interests. Job shadows at local businesses extend these career exploration experiences. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Pre-Technology Education, STEM Math, STEM Science, Physical Education and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).
courses.prerequisites: Admission to GMTCC is competitive. Students must demonstrate a clear and reasonable path to graduation in order to be accepted for admission.
courses.fulfills_text: Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Pre-Technology Education, STEM Math, STEM Science, Physical Education and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: ALLIED HEALTH introduces students to careers in the healthcare field, which are among the fastest growing, both locally and nationally. Students who successfully complete the program meet entry-level requirements for a number of careers in the healthcare industry. They have the opportunity to earn a number of professional certifications including; Licensed Nursing Assistant (LNA), Emergency Medical Responder (EMR), Personal Care Attendant (PCA), First Aid and CPR, Mental Health First Aid, and OSHA-10. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Allied Health, Science, Art, Health and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: AUTOMOTIVE TECHNOLOGY provides opportunities to experience the latest high-tech equipment located in a state-of-the-art facility and is modeled after the Vermont General Service Technician Program. Students in this program receive theory instruction and hands-on performance in all Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) areas (Brakes, Steering and Suspension; Alignment; Manual Transmissions and Transaxles; and Electrical Systems), which provide initial training for employment in the automotive service field or further training at a post-secondary institution. In order to successfully complete the program, students must pass the General Service Technician exam. College credit is awarded from Central Maine Community College and through articulation agreements with Ohio Technical College, Lincoln Technical Institute, Universal Technical Institute (UTI) and University of Northwestern Ohio. Students also have advanced placement agreements with all New Hampshire Technical Colleges and may earn VADA General Service Technician (GST) and S/P2, Mechanical Repair Safety professional certifications. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Automotive Technology, Math, Science, Health and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).
courses.prerequisites: Admission to GMTCC is competitive. Students must demonstrate a clear and reasonable path to graduation in order to be accepted for admission.
courses.fulfills_text: Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Automotive Technology, Math, Science, Health and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION is a strong pathway for students who want to understand business practices and potentially own their own business someday. Accounting principles, small business administration/management, personal finance, computer applications and entrepreneurship are the focus. Leadership skills are fostered through teamwork and collaboration in an office environment. As part of this program, students are expected to participate in two internship experiences with local businesses. College credit may be earned from Vermont Technical College with articulation agreements at Northern Vermont University. In addition, students may obtain professional certifications. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Business Administration, Math and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).
courses.prerequisites: Admission to GMTCC is competitive. Students must demonstrate a clear and reasonable path to graduation in order to be accepted for admission.
courses.fulfills_text: Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Business Administration, Math and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: COMPUTER NETWORKING TECHNOLOGY provides full day and half day opportunities for students to install, configure, and troubleshoot Windows, Apple, and Linux operating systems. Cyber Security Fundamentals and Programming Fundamentals are also introduced. Students can successfully complete the CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+ and Server+ professional certification requirements. Students will also be able to earn the FAA Commercial Drone License. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Studies, Computer Networking Technology, Math, Science, Health and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: CONSTRUCTION TECHNOLOGY provides training in all phases of residential construction. Students plan and participate in the construction of a complete modular home; mastering structural framing techniques, window installation, siding, roofing, and finish work while working collaboratively with electricians and plumbers at the job site. Students visit commercial job sites and experience an introduction to commercial construction methods, while gaining professional certifications in OSHA-10 and National Center for Construction Education and Research (NCCER). Students also earn college credits through Central Maine Community College. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Construction Technology, Math, Art, Health, Physical Education and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: CREATIVE MEDIA ART & DESIGN is where students explore graphic design, illustration, photography, animation, fine art, and filmmaking, in preparation for college and entry-level positions in a variety of businesses including; advertising and design companies, TV stations, and film production companies. Over the course of the year, students create a comprehensive portfolio to showcase their work and may earn Adobe Certified Associate Credentials. In addition, they may earn up to 12 college credits through Community College of Vermont. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Media Arts, Visual Arts, Math and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: CULINARY ARTS is designed for students who plan on exploring a career as a Chef, Cook, Baker, Pastry Chef, Dining Room Manager, etc. Study will include the fundamentals and concepts that apply to culinary arts with an emphasis on the understanding of the technology and creative skills needed for success in this evolving career. The course consists of lectures, demonstrations and practical experiences in all aspects of a student-operated commercial kitchen and dining room. Students may earn college credits through Central Maine Community College and articulations through Culinary Institute of American in addition to S/P2 and ServSafe certifications. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Culinary Arts, Math, Science, Art, Health and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: ELECTRICAL TECHNOLOGY provides training in all phases of residential and commercial wiring. Students receive instruction in safe and proper operation of tools and power equipment, reading electrical plans and specifications, and employability skills required in a 21st century work environment. Students experience wiring residential and commercial structures, introduction to energy saving techniques and alternative energy sources. Students are prepared for the successful completion of the Vermont Electrical Apprenticeship I & II exams and earn an OSHA-10 professional certification. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Electrical Technology, Math, Science, Art, Health and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: ENGINEERING incorporates advanced technologies through project-based learning. Students engage in Project Lead the Way’s nationally recognized Pathway to Engineering, applying the design process and gaining skills in problem-solving, communication, and teamwork. Coursework includes Introduction to Engineering Design and Principles of Engineering.
courses.prerequisites: Admission to GMTCC is competitive. Students must demonstrate a clear and reasonable path to graduation in order to be accepted for admission.

courses.description: FORESTRY & LAND MANAGEMENT students will learn introductory and basic training in areas of forest products, natural resource management, wood production, value added wood products, and the technologies associated with these applications. Modern maple sugaring techniques, tree identification, forest ecology, forest pest and diseases, forest management, safe timber harvesting practices, and techniques of reforestation are emphasized. All students will test for Loggers Education and Advancement of Professionalism (LEAP), Game of Logging, Logger's First Aid & Rescue and Vermont Professional Logger’s Program certifications, as well as OSHA-10 and UVM tractor safety. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Forestry & Land Management, Math, Science, Health, Physical Education and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: HEATING, VENTILATION & AIR CONDITIONING offers entry level training in residential and commercial heating, air conditioning, and refrigerant systems. Students learn about refrigeration physics and the refrigeration cycle, combustion theory, oil and gas fuel systems, air distribution systems, air conditioning and heating systems, wiring diagrams, piping practices, soldering, brazing, systematic troubleshooting and basic electrical theory related to HVAC. Students may earn professional certifications in OSHA-10, National Oilheat Research Alliance (NORA) Bronze Oilheat Technician, EPA Act 608 Safe Refrigerant Handling and OSHA-10. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration, Math, Science, Health, Physical Education and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).

courses.description: SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE & FOOD SYSTEMS is designed to help students obtain knowledge and skills in the diversified field of agriculture and food systems, including but not limited to; soil science, livestock care, horticulture, organic practices, dairy, land management, product making and marketing, agricultural mechanics, entrepreneurship, farmyard construction, HVAC, farm technology and alternative energies for agriculture. Students may earn First Aid & CPR, OSHA-10, UVM Tractor Safety, Game of Logging and Servsafe professional certifications. Students have the opportunity to earn proficiencies in English and Literacy, Global Citizenship, Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems, Math, Science, Art, Health, Physical Education and Employability Skills (Transferable Skills).
